Resumarc
Free resume and CV builder with ATS-ready templates and one-time passes
Resumarc is a web-based resume and cover letter builder with over 100 resume templates and 20 cover letter templates made to work well with applicant tracking systems. It offers a guided editor with writing suggestions based on O*NET data for 1,016 occupations, a resume checker that scores documents against ATS criteria with section-by-section feedback, and over 80 complete resume examples by job title. The builder, TXT export, and a daily AI suggestion allowance are free. PDF and DOCX export and larger AI allowances are available as one-time passes with a 14-day refund policy.

Inwista
Professional subtitles in 70+ languages with an API
Professional subtitles in over 70 languages from any audio or video file. Broadcast-grade formatting is available in one click, along with an accurate transcript that includes speaker labels. Everything stays in one project. You can style the captions to match your brand, translate them, and cut the video by deleting text, since the timeline follows the transcript. Export SRT, VTT, DOCX, or a finished video with captions burned in, or push it directly to Drive, Dropbox, YouTube, or Vimeo. A public REST API and signed webhooks let you run the whole system from your own software, with an official n8n template if you'd rather not write code.

AI-native, privacy-first task management that understands natural typing
Todoless is an AI-native task and project app for professionals, freelancers, and small teams. Its on-device parser turns plain sentences like "Call Sara tomorrow 3pm #work 30min" into structured tasks instantly, in English, German, and Italian, with nothing sent to a server. It works fully offline, syncs across iOS, Android, and web, and is Swiss-made and privacy-first. The team is also building toward Task Decay: an AI that clears tasks once they stop mattering.

DOFOTT
Automatic travel time blocks added to Google Calendar events
DOFOTT adds travel time to Google Calendar automatically. Connect your Google account once, set your home and work addresses, and every event with a location gets a travel block timed with real Google Maps durations for driving, transit, cycling, or walking. It handles recurring events, routes directly between back-to-back meetings when that's shorter, and adds an optional parking buffer. Travel blocks are regular Google Calendar events, visible in Apple Calendar, Notion Calendar, and anywhere else that reads your account. Booking links like Calendly also show the time as busy.
Free during beta; after that, free for 12 travel meetings a month, $5 if you go over, or $36 per year.
